From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finbank.com>, alyssa.reed@finbank.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Throughput stratified evaluation + unit economics — MAP milestones

Sam — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short plan and the initial CSV from our sustained runs. High level answers up front:

- Sustained QPS (32 concurrent callers, 450 tokens median):
  - gptf-13B-latent (int8 quant): ~38-44 sustained QPS, ~980-1,200 tokens/sec aggregate on a 4xA100-80GB pool (sharded runtime).
  - gptf-3.5-lite (int4): ~160-200 sustained QPS, ~1,800-2,300 tokens/sec aggregate on 2xA100 or 8xV100 equivalent (lower memory footprint allowed more concurrency).

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) typical: gptf-13B ~95-130ms; gptf-3.5-lite ~30-60ms (depends on cold vs warmed KV cache).

- Concurrency behavior: beyond 32 callers, latency percentiles for gptf-13B start to grow linearly unless batching windows are increased — we recommend soft limits >48 should use autoscale bursts.

- Prefix/KV caching: yes — your session affinity means prefix caching will apply and reduces per-call compute by ~12-18% for repeat prompt prefixes (we measured on your representative prompt set).

Attached CSV contains the raw sustained runs we executed 2026-11-07. I also included three unit-econ scenarios in the PDF: conservative (no caching), baseline (expected caching delta), and optimistic (higher batching).

Next steps proposed (MAP milestones):
1) 2026-11-10: FinBank provides final 50 sample prompts + traffic shape (hourly QPS) — you already agreed to share these.
2) 2026-11-12: Redwood runs expanded sustained test at 72-hour window (to capture diurnal effects).
3) 2026-11-17: Joint review — final QPS and token-cost per call signoff.
4) 2026-11-24: Procurement/commit and Dedicated capacity provisioning.

Rishi & Marissa — please review the concurrency recommendations and confirm autoscale/burst sizing and estimated monthly committed spend for the baseline scenario.

Best,
Dylan
AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rbw-map-throughput-plan-v1.xlsx (plan), finbank-sustained-qps-results-20261108.csv (raw results), token-econ-scenarios-attachment.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput stratified evaluation + unit economics — MAP milestones

Quick read: plan looks solid. A couple of operational clarifications and a revised costing ballpark: 

- Autoscale math: for baseline concurrency 32 we recommend a reserved pool equivalent to 4xA100-80GB with a burst policy of +50% for 30 minutes (burst governed by request token budget). If FinBank wants >99.9% p95 SLO at peak, bump reserved to 6xA100.

- Unit economics (baseline assumptions):
  - Model inference cost per million tokens (our hosted pricing equivalents for internal calc): gptf-13B-int8 => $16 / M tokens; gptf-3.5-lite-int4 => $6.50 / M tokens.
  - For FinBank median 450 tokens/call: gptf-13B => $0.0072 / call; gptf-3.5-lite => $0.002925 / call.
  - For 95th (1,800 tokens): gptf-13B => $0.0288 / call; gptf-3.5-lite => $0.0117 / call.

- Recommendation: prioritize gptf-3.5-lite for high-frequency low-cost paths and reserve gptf-13B for high-recall flows (manual review / escalation). Use model routing rules in the MAP to fall back to gptf-3.5-lite when latency budgets tighten.

- Question for infra: does FinBank need HIPAA/SOC-level logging for requests? If so we need to schedule Private deployment steps earlier in the MAP (adds ~3 weeks to provisioning lead).

I updated the spreadsheet with cost lines and the autoscale policy; attaching the updated workbook.

- Rishi
Sr. Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rbw-map-throughput-plan-v1.xlsx (updated with costing and autoscale rows)
